industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): technology saw $5.5 billion of net selling in the week, the most since January 2025 (Jefferies, 17 Oct), the rotation came out of it, and Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made'; against that, Jefferies finds sector pockets still upgrading inside it (analogue chips, optical networking, artificial-intelligence memory) and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, B prior at industry level, carried by Semiconductors at A. The industry row stays C because the industry is split: Semiconductors (D), Software B2B Enterprise (D), Fintech (D) and Games (D) carry the Underweight; IT services, Hardware and vertical software stay Neutral. Counter-case for D: the heaviest net selling in 21 months is a regime statement; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged, with the sector now split by the sources. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): artificial-intelligence-linked semiconductors fell eight straight sessions to 16 Oct, technology net selling was the heaviest since January 2025, Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made', Korea fell about 20% in October on de-grossing, and the AI credits that set this row (the neoclouds) are 'the epicentre of the funding cost debate' (Goldman, 19 Oct); against it, Jefferies (22 Oct) is 'incrementally positive' on analogue chips with a read-across to Infineon and STMicroelectronics, sees China's equipment imports up 26% as the upside for 2027-28, and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive, while on equipment Jefferies' own headline is 'ASML - Still not excited'. Neither condition for C is met (no stabilisation read on the AI credits; no sell-side buy call on the European sector). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior, the disagreement stated: the market still ranks the sector first while cutting its multiple. Ten of the 149 Pool stocks. Counter-case: the analogue upcycle 'has more legs' into 2027, demand was never the problem, and a D on ten Pool names pushes the Lists away from the one European industry with upgrades; the analogue read is a reason to look at STMicroelectronics stock by stock, not to move a row that is mostly equipment.

memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage Assessment, medium conviction, no capital and no position view. Direction stated in the memo: neutral on the business and neutral on the equity at EUR 70.75, which is why the recommendation is progress rather than buy. The recommendation departs deliberately from the risks family, which recommends parking. That family states: "Stage progression recommendation: Park the Melexis investment case immediately until Chinese pricing pressure abates and local foundry yields stabilize; Melexis trades at 21x PER 2027F, close to its historical ten-year median multiple, and lowered CAGR targets from 10% to high single digits limit long-term re-rating potential." Its meta-analysis section repeats that the aggregated conclusion is to park until local foundry yields and margin recovery are verified. The memo departs on dated evidence rather than on judgement. The risks family report was produced 27 June 2026. Melexis reported second-quarter 2026 results on 29 July 2026, and the earnings-review family covering that print was produced 13 August 2026, seven weeks later. The risks family named one test above all others: "The single most critical re-pre-mortem trigger is any failure of gross margin to expand to 40% in H1-26" (attributed to Bernstein). First-half 2026 gross margin was 40.2% and second-quarter gross margin 40.5%. That test was passed.
case: The case rests on four linked propositions, in the memo's own order.

First, the operating trough is confirmed rather than forecast. Two consecutive quarters now evidence the turn. Second-quarter 2026 revenue of EUR 217.1m beat consensus by 3.2% and grew 7% sequentially; gross margin reached 40.5%, up 150 basis points year on year; operating profit rose 8% year on year and 16% sequentially; earnings per share came in above consensus. The beat spanned every line of the income statement, and it was struck against external consensus rather than against management's own lowered bar. Third-quarter guidance of EUR 220m to EUR 225m came 2.1% above the EUR 218m consensus, and first-half revenue of EUR 419.2m topped management's own flat guidance. Jefferies states automotive inventory destocking has officially concluded. Bernstein records distributor inventories clean and flat, arguing that sequential growth reflects genuine end-market vehicle production rather than channel loading.

Second, the internal change force is a permanent unit-cost reduction already banked. Poor-yield wafers held in inventory created a 200 basis-point gross-margin drag in late 2025. The chief financial officer confirms the fault is resolved in manufacturing tests and states the resulting gain carries zero execution risk against guided targets. The proof is in the sequence: gross margin moved from 38.6% for FY25 to 39.9% in the first quarter and 40.5% in the second. Alongside it sit the China restructuring, a Shanghai wholly foreign-owned enterprise established March 2026 transacting in renminbi, fully operational local outsourced assembly and test for lighting, latch and switch lines, and completed initial silicon tape-outs with local 12-inch foundries.
counter_case: The counter-case is carried at full force in the memo and is the reason conviction is medium rather than high.

The risks family recommends parking, and says so twice. Its stated recommendation is to park the Melexis investment case immediately until Chinese pricing pressure abates and local foundry yields stabilise, noting that Melexis trades at 21x 2027 forecast earnings, close to its historical ten-year median, and that lowered growth targets limit long-term re-rating potential. Its meta-analysis section repeats the conclusion. Its analysis-of-competing-hypotheses matrix scores the False Friend profile the outright winner at one disconfirming item against nine for the bullish profile and four for the bearish; the pre-mortem version of the same framework gives two hard structural inconsistencies for False Friend against eight and four. It puts sector base rates for similar analog semiconductor transitions at a 65% joint failure probability over 18 to 24 months, with false friends comprising 20% of identified failure narratives.
triggers: Named next-stage questions, six. Decompose the gross-margin bridge from 40.5% to the 45% target into yield, mix, volume and price, since the entire earnings case sits in those 450 basis points. Establish whether strategic inventory can fall toward EUR 200m without write-downs, given it peaked at EUR 300.3m at roughly 204 days of sales. Test the 2027 pricing round, the first without long-term agreement cover. Reconcile the three conflicting X-FAB dependency figures, at 40%, 40% to 55% and about 80% of wafer requirements, against primary filings. Quantify the revenue at risk from Chinese domestic substitution, sizing the mature-node, low-complexity portion of the portfolio separately. Assess whether the 133% payout ratio forces a dividend decision if the recovery slips.
Valuation work deferred. Element E3 (Sufficient total-shareholder-return / valuation upside) is first assessed at Early-Stage Assessment and the memo deliberately does not pre-empt it.
Timeline. Early-Stage Assessment pickup after the third-quarter print in October 2026, which delivers the first clean read on the 41% gross-margin guide.

Reassessment criteria if parked instead, four. Gross margin reaching 41% or better in the second half of 2026, observable in the February 2027 release. Strategic inventory falling below EUR 200m, observable quarterly on the balance sheet. The 2027 annual price negotiation delivering declines inside the 3% to 4% historical norm, observable in early 2027. Chinese vendor share of China automotive semiconductors not rising above 25%, observable in annual industry share data.
Bullish trigger. Gross margin above 42% with strategic inventory below EUR 250m in the same quarter, which would refute both remaining false friends at once.
Bearish trigger. A second-half gross margin below 40% combined with a further Chinese share gain, which would confirm the structural rather than cyclical reading.
